intent.raw_query: Swiss Alps ski holiday family, $7000, 7 days, February

experiences.name: Zermatt Ski Safari
experiences.description: Explore the world-renowned ski slopes of Zermatt with access to over 360km of pistes across Switzerland and Italy. Ski beneath the iconic Matterhorn with breathtaking panoramic views. Suitable for intermediate to advanced skiers with varied terrain including groomed runs and off-piste adventures.

experiences.name: Jungfrau Region Snowshoeing & Winter Hiking
experiences.description: Guided snowshoeing tour through the stunning Jungfrau region, trekking through pristine alpine landscapes, frozen lakes, and snow-covered forests. Visit the Aletsch Glacier viewpoint, the largest glacier in the Alps, and enjoy a traditional Swiss fondue lunch at a mountain hut along the trail.

experiences.name: St. Moritz Ice Skating & Bobsled Experience
experiences.description: Skate on the legendary frozen Lake St. Moritz and then experience the thrill of riding the historic Olympia Bob Run, one of the world's oldest natural ice bobsled tracks dating back to 1904. A unique adrenaline-pumping winter activity combining culture and sport in the glamorous St. Moritz setting.

experiences.name: Glacier 3000 Suspension Bridge & Peak Walk
experiences.description: Take the cable car up to Glacier 3000 and walk across the Peak Walk by Tissot, the world's first suspension bridge connecting two mountain peaks at 3,000 meters altitude. Enjoy 360-degree views of 24 Alpine peaks including Mont Blanc and the Matterhorn, and optionally try the glacier ski area or snow bus ride.

experiences.name: Traditional Swiss Alpine Cuisine & Cheese Cellar Tour
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in authentic Swiss mountain culture with a guided visit to a traditional alpine cheese cellar in the Appenzell region, learning how Gruyère and Raclette are crafted. Follow with a hands-on fondue and raclette cooking class paired with local Swiss wines and schnapps in a cozy chalet setting.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Swiss Alps, Switzerland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Zurich or Milan Malpensa airport at 22:30. Take a regional train or bus toward Poschiavo. Check in to B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama upon late arrival. Settle in, unpack, and rest for the week ahead.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In transit
meals.lunch: N/A - In transit
meals.dinner: Grab a quick sandwich or snack at the airport arrivals hall or a vending machine (~CHF 8-12). Most restaurants will be closed upon late arrival in Poschiavo.

day_by_day.notes: Poschiavo is best reached via the Bernina Express rail line from St. Moritz or by bus from Tirano (Italy). Pre-book your train ticket in advance on SBB.ch for best budget fares. The journey from Zurich takes approximately 3.5-4 hours. Confirm check-in arrangements with the B&B for late arrival. Keep CHF cash on hand as rural areas may have limited card acceptance.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a hearty B&B breakfast included with your stay. Afterward, take a leisurely walk through the charming historic village of Poschiavo — explore the Piazza Comunale, the Spanish Quarter (Quartiere Spagnolo), and the Collegiate Church of San Vittore. This orientation walk is completely free and gives you a feel for the local Romansh-Italian culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearby Lago di Poschiavo (Lake Poschiavo), a scenic frozen or semi-frozen alpine lake in winter. Walk along the lakeside path (~3 km loop, free). If conditions allow, enjoy the stunning mountain reflections and snow-covered surroundings. Visit the local Coop supermarket in Poschiavo to stock up on budget groceries, snacks, and water for the week.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the B&B and relax. Explore the village in the early evening — the illuminated historic buildings are beautiful in winter. Plan your ski days for the rest of the week by researching Diavolezza and Corvatsch ski areas accessible via the Bernina Express.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B Berninahaus Panorama — enjoy local bread, cheese, cold cuts, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Self-catered picnic with groceries from Coop Poschiavo — bread, local cheese, salami, and fruit (~CHF 8-10).
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal using B&B kitchen facilities if available, or try Ristorante Croce Federale in Poschiavo for a budget pasta or risotto dish (~CHF 18-22). Ask for the daily special (piatto del giorno) for best value.

day_by_day.notes: Poschiavo sits at 1,014m elevation. Dress in warm layers even in the village. The Bernina Express scenic railway passes through Poschiavo — a free visual treat from the platform. Exchange currency or use ATMs in the village center. Budget tip: buy a 7-day Swiss Half Fare Card or regional Engadin pass for discounted train travel.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Bernina Express train from Poschiavo toward Pontresina/St. Moritz (approx. 45-60 min, ~CHF 15-20 one way with Half Fare Card). Head to Diavolezza ski area — one of the most spectacular and budget-accessible ski resorts in the Engadin valley. Purchase a day ski pass (~CHF 55-65 with discounts). Ski the wide open glacier runs on Diavolezza with breathtaking views of Piz Palü and Morteratsch Glacier.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing at Diavolezza. Try the famous Diavolezza-Lagalb traverse run if conditions permit — a classic 10km off-piste route (guide recommended). Alternatively, stick to groomed blue and red pistes for intermediate skiers. Take a break at the mid-mountain restaurant terrace with packed lunch to save money.
day_by_day.evening: Return by train to Poschiavo. Warm up with a hot drink at the B&B. Rest tired muscles and prepare gear for the next ski day.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B — fuel up well before a full ski day.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from B&B or Coop — sandwiches, energy bars, thermos of hot tea (~CHF 5-8). Mountain restaurant prices are very high (CHF 20-35 per meal), so packing lunch saves significantly.
meals.dinner: Trattoria da Reto or a local pizzeria in Poschiavo — pizza or pasta (~CHF 16-20). Alternatively, self-cater with pasta and local sauce from Coop (~CHF 5-7).

day_by_day.notes: Diavolezza ski pass: check for online early-booking discounts at diavolezza.ch. Ski rental in Poschiavo or Pontresina is cheaper than at the resort base — budget ~CHF 30-40/day for skis, boots, and poles. Bring your own helmet if possible. The Bernina Express train schedule is limited — check SBB.ch for exact times and book ahead. Dress in full waterproof ski gear; temperatures at 3,000m can drop to -15°C or below.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning — allow muscles to recover. After B&B breakfast, take a snowshoe hike from Poschiavo toward the Alp Grüm area. The trail from Poschiavo station up toward Alp Grüm (accessible also by Bernina Express) offers stunning winter panoramas over the Valposchiavo valley. Snowshoe rental available locally (~CHF 15-20/day).
day_by_day.afternoon: Board the Bernina Express to Alp Grüm station (one of the most scenic stops in Europe, ~CHF 10-15 with Half Fare Card). Walk the short snowshoe loop around Alp Grüm with views of Palü Glacier. Visit the historic Ristorante Alp Grüm for a warm drink (hot chocolate ~CHF 5). Return to Poschiavo by train in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Poschiavo's evening atmosphere. Visit the local Enoteca or wine bar for a glass of Valtellina red wine — the valley's famous Nebbiolo-based wine produced just across the Italian border (~CHF 5-8/glass). Early night to prepare for another ski day.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the snowshoe trail — thermos soup, sandwiches, chocolate (~CHF 5-8).
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner at B&B — buy local Pizzoccheri pasta (a Valtellina buckwheat specialty) from Coop and cook it yourself (~CHF 6-8 for ingredients). This is an authentic regional dish and very budget-friendly.

day_by_day.notes: Alp Grüm sits at 2,091m and offers one of the most dramatic viewpoints on the Bernina line. The snowshoe trails are generally well-marked but check local conditions at the Poschiavo tourist office (free maps available). This is a great low-cost active day that showcases the alpine scenery without ski pass expenses. Bring trekking poles for stability on icy paths.

day_by_day.morning: Second ski day — take the Bernina Express to Pontresina and connect to Corvatsch or Corviglia ski areas above St. Moritz. Corviglia is more budget-friendly and beginner-to-intermediate friendly. Day pass ~CHF 60-70 (check for online discounts). Enjoy wide groomed pistes with views over the Engadin lakes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing at Corviglia. Try the long Marguns run back to Celerina for a scenic descent. If budget allows, take the cable car up to Piz Nair (3,057m) for panoramic views of the entire Upper Engadin valley — even non-skiers can appreciate this viewpoint.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo by Bernina Express. Treat yourself to a sit-down dinner to celebrate the halfway point of your trip. Try the local Grotto-style restaurant in Poschiavo for authentic Graubünden cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B — eat heartily before skiing.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch again to save on mountain restaurant costs (~CHF 5-8). Find a sunny terrace spot on the mountain to enjoy your meal with a view.
meals.dinner: Grotto-style dinner at a local Poschiavo restaurant — try Capuns (Swiss chard rolls with spätzle) or Maluns (potato dish) for authentic Graubünden flavors (~CHF 20-25 including a local beer or wine).

day_by_day.notes: St. Moritz is one of the world's most famous ski resorts but can be explored on a budget by focusing on skiing and avoiding the luxury shops and restaurants. The Engadin ski pass covers multiple areas — check if a 2-day or 3-day pass offers better value than individual day passes. Friday slopes may be busier as weekend visitors arrive — start early to beat crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Active morning — try cross-country skiing (Langlauf) on the famous Engadin Ski Marathon trail network near Pontresina or S-chanf. Cross-country ski pass and rental is significantly cheaper than downhill (~CHF 10-15 trail pass, ~CHF 20-25 rental). The Engadin valley floor offers 200km of groomed cross-country trails with spectacular mountain scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Poschiavo by early afternoon. Visit the Museo di Poschiavo (local history museum, ~CHF 5 entry) to learn about the valley's unique Romansh-Italian culture, the Bernina railway history, and local traditions. Afterward, take a final walk around the village and pick up souvenirs — local honey, Valtellina wine, or Bündner Nusstorte (nut tart) from the local bakery.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Poschiavo. Splurge slightly on a proper sit-down meal at the best local restaurant. Try Brasato al Vino Rosso (beef braised in red wine) or local trout from the valley streams.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the cross-country ski trails — energy bars, sandwiches, hot tea (~CHF 5-8).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Ristorante Croce Federale or Hotel Albrici restaurant in Poschiavo — budget CHF 25-35 for a two-course meal with local wine. This is your splurge meal of the trip — well deserved!

day_by_day.notes: The Engadin Ski Marathon (world-famous 42km cross-country race) takes place in mid-March — if your dates overlap, the atmosphere is incredible even as a spectator. Saturday is the busiest day on the slopes — cross-country skiing avoids the downhill crowds entirely. The Museo di Poschiavo is small but charming and provides great cultural context for the valley. Buy Bündner Nusstorte from the local bakery as an edible souvenir — it travels well.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — enjoy a leisurely last B&B breakfast. Take a short morning walk through Poschiavo village one last time, visiting the Sunday market if available. Pack your bags and check out. Take a final look at the stunning Bernina massif from the village square.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight/train, take the scenic Bernina Express one final time northward toward St. Moritz and Chur, or southward toward Tirano (Italy) for connections to Milan. The Bernina Express itself is a UNESCO World Heritage railway — enjoy every moment of the journey through viaducts, spiral tunnels, and glacial landscapes as your final Swiss Alps experience.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Switzerland with incredible memories of skiing, snowshoeing, and alpine culture in one of Europe's most beautiful and authentic mountain valleys.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B — final Swiss breakfast with local cheese and bread.
meals.lunch: Grab a Bündner Nusstorte and local snacks from the bakery for the train journey (~CHF 8-10). The Bernina Express has a dining car but it is expensive — packed food is the budget choice.
meals.dinner: Airport or transit meal depending on departure schedule (~CHF 15-20 at airport, or pack remaining groceries from Coop).

day_by_day.notes: Check out time at B&B — confirm with hosts. The Bernina Express requires a seat reservation (~CHF 10-15) even with a rail pass — book in advance on SBB.ch as it sells out quickly, especially on weekends. If departing via Milan Malpensa, the Tirano-Milan train connection takes approximately 2.5 hours. If departing via Zurich, allow 3.5-4 hours travel time. Budget summary for the week: accommodation ~CHF 350-450 (7 nights B&B), ski passes ~CHF 180-200 (3 ski days), transport ~CHF 80-100, food ~CHF 150-180, activities ~CHF 40-60. Total estimated budget: CHF 800-1,000 per person for 7 days — excellent value for the Swiss Alps.

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival. Flight UA lands at 22:30. Transfer from airport to B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama. Check in, settle into your room, and get a good night's rest.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — travel day.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama around 23:30–00:00 depending on transfer. Grab a light snack if available at the B&B or from any provisions you carry. Rest and prepare for the week ahead.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: N/A — in transit / airport dining
meals.dinner: Light snack at the B&B or airport meal before departure. Keep it simple — a sandwich or airport bistro meal.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange your transfer from the airport to Poschiavo in advance. The drive from Zurich Airport to Poschiavo is approximately 2.5–3 hours. Consider hiring a private transfer or renting a car. Confirm late check-in with the B&B ahead of time. Pack light layers for the cold alpine arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a leisurely B&B breakfast and take your first morning to orient yourself in Poschiavo. Stroll through the charming historic village center of Poschiavo, admiring the Spanish Quarter architecture and the frozen Lago di Poschiavo. This gentle introduction helps you acclimatize to the altitude before more strenuous activities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearby Livigno ski area (approximately 45 minutes from Poschiavo via the Bernina Pass road) for an introductory afternoon ski session. Livigno offers excellent beginner-to-intermediate slopes and is a great warm-up destination. Rent ski equipment on-site if needed. Enjoy the wide, well-groomed pistes with stunning alpine panoramas.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo by early evening. Explore the village and enjoy a relaxed dinner at a local restaurant in town.

meals.breakfast: Full B&B breakfast at Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama — expect fresh bread, cold cuts, cheese, yogurt, and hot drinks. Included with stay.
meals.lunch: Mountain restaurant lunch at Livigno ski area — try a hearty plate of pasta or a local mountain soup (pizzoccheri, a buckwheat pasta dish typical of the Valtellina region). Budget CHF 20–35.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ristorante Suisse or a local trattoria in Poschiavo village. Try regional specialties like pizzoccheri, polenta with cheese, or braised venison. Budget CHF 35–55 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Check road conditions on the Bernina Pass (SS38/Route 29) before driving to Livigno — winter chains or snow tires are mandatory. Livigno is technically in Italy but easily accessible. Bring your passport. Altitude in this region is around 1,800–2,000m, so stay hydrated and apply high-SPF sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Embark on the Traditional Swiss Alpine Cuisine & Cheese Cellar Tour. Travel to a nearby alpine cheese producer in the Engadin Valley (approximately 30–45 minutes from Poschiavo via the Bernina Pass toward St. Moritz). Enjoy a guided tour of a traditional cheese cellar, learn about Swiss alpine dairy culture, and sample local cheeses, cured meats, and homemade jams.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the cheese tour, continue into the Upper Engadin region and visit the area around Pontresina or Diavolezza. Take the Diavolezza cable car up to 2,978m for breathtaking panoramic views of the Bernina massif and Morteratsch Glacier. If conditions allow, enjoy a beginner-friendly ski run or simply soak in the spectacular mountain scenery from the summit terrace.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo for the evening. Relax at the B&B and enjoy a quieter night in.

meals.breakfast: B&B breakfast at Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama.
meals.lunch: Included as part of the Cheese Cellar Tour — a traditional alpine spread of local cheeses, bread, cold cuts, and regional condiments. A truly authentic mid-range experience.
meals.dinner: Self-catered or light dinner at the B&B if available, or pick up local provisions from a Poschiavo village shop (Coop or local deli). Try local bread, cheese, and charcuterie for a cozy in-room meal. Budget CHF 15–25.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Traditional Swiss Alpine Cuisine & Cheese Cellar Tour in advance as group sizes are often limited. The Diavolezza cable car costs approximately CHF 40–50 return. Dress in warm layers — summit temperatures can be -10°C to -20°C with wind chill. The Bernina Express train also runs through this region and offers a scenic alternative for part of the journey.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion: St. Moritz Ice Skating & Bobsled Experience. Depart early from Poschiavo toward St. Moritz (approximately 45 minutes via the Bernina Pass). Begin your morning with ice skating on the legendary frozen Lake St. Moritz — one of the most iconic winter experiences in the Alps. Skate rental is available on-site. The lake setting surrounded by snow-capped peaks is absolutely magical.
day_by_day.afternoon: After lunch, experience the thrill of riding the historic Cresta Run or the Olympic Bobsled Run in St. Moritz. The bobsled experience allows guests to ride as a passenger with a professional pilot on the world's oldest natural ice bobsled track. This is a bucket-list winter sports moment. Book your bobsled slot in advance as availability is limited.
day_by_day.evening: Explore St. Moritz village in the early evening — browse the luxury boutiques, admire the glamorous atmosphere, and enjoy the vibrant après-ski scene before heading back to Poschiavo.

meals.breakfast: B&B breakfast before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch in St. Moritz — try Café Bar Hauser or a mid-range mountain bistro. Enjoy a rösti, fondue, or a hearty soup. Budget CHF 25–40 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner back in Poschiavo at a local restaurant. Try Ristorante Albrici, a historic establishment in the village known for regional Graubünden cuisine. Budget CHF 40–60 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The St. Moritz Ice Skating & Bobsled Experience must be pre-booked. The bobsled ride costs approximately CHF 150–200 per person. Ice skating on the lake is free or low-cost with skate rental around CHF 10–15. St. Moritz is a luxury resort town — budget accordingly for any additional spending. Drive carefully on the Bernina Pass in winter conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion: Zermatt Ski Safari. Depart early from Poschiavo for Zermatt (approximately 3–3.5 hours by car/train via Chur or the Glacier Express route). Arrive in Zermatt — a car-free village — and begin your ski safari across the world-renowned 360km+ piste network. The Matterhorn backdrop makes every run unforgettable. Ski guides are available to help you navigate the vast terrain.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing across Zermatt's interconnected ski areas — Rothorn, Gornergrat, and Klein Matterhorn (the highest ski area in the Alps at 3,883m). Intermediate skiers will love the long, sweeping red runs, while advanced skiers can tackle challenging black pistes. Take a break at a mountain restaurant for a mid-afternoon snack.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Zermatt's famous après-ski atmosphere at a village bar before catching the train back. Given the long travel day, consider staying overnight in Zermatt if budget allows, or return to Poschiavo by late evening.

meals.breakfast: Early B&B breakfast or grab a pastry and coffee at a bakery en route.
meals.lunch: Mountain restaurant lunch on the Zermatt slopes — try Chez Vrony or a mid-mountain hut for traditional Swiss mountain food. Rösti, raclette, or a warming goulash soup. Budget CHF 30–50.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Zermatt village before departure — try Restaurant Whymper-Stube for classic Swiss fondue and raclette in a cozy, authentic setting. Budget CHF 40–65 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Zermatt is a long day trip from Poschiavo. Consider taking the Bernina Express to Chur and then connecting trains to Zermatt for a scenic rail experience (book in advance). Alternatively, drive to Täsch (the last car-accessible village) and take the shuttle train into Zermatt. Lift passes for Zermatt cost approximately CHF 80–100 per day. Book the Zermatt Ski Safari guide in advance for the best experience.

day_by_day.morning: Jungfrau Region Snowshoeing & Winter Hiking — a full-day excursion to the Jungfrau region (approximately 3 hours from Poschiavo via train through Chur and Interlaken). Join a guided snowshoeing tour through the pristine alpine landscapes around Grindelwald or Wengen. Trek through snow-covered forests, open meadows, and dramatic mountain terrain with the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau as your backdrop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the snowshoeing tour into the afternoon, exploring higher terrain and enjoying panoramic viewpoints. The guide will share insights about the local flora, fauna, and alpine culture. This is a wonderful contrast to the high-speed ski days — peaceful, immersive, and deeply connected to the mountain environment.
day_by_day.evening: Return journey to Poschiavo by train. Arrive back at the B&B by late evening. Enjoy a quiet final full evening at the accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Early B&B breakfast before departure.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch provided by the snowshoeing tour guide, or stop at a mountain hut along the trail for a warm soup and bread. Budget CHF 15–25 if not included.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Grindelwald or Interlaken before the return journey — try Restaurant Onkel Tom's Hütte in Grindelwald for hearty Swiss mountain food. Budget CHF 35–55 per person. Alternatively, grab a light meal at the train station restaurant.

day_by_day.notes: The Jungfrau Region Snowshoeing & Winter Hiking tour must be pre-booked. Snowshoes and poles are typically provided by the guide. Wear waterproof, insulated boots and dress in breathable layers. The Jungfrau region is a UNESCO World Heritage Site — a truly special experience. Train connections from Poschiavo via the Bernina Express are scenic and comfortable; book rail tickets in advance on SBB.ch.

day_by_day.morning: Glacier 3000 Suspension Bridge & Peak Walk. Travel from Poschiavo toward Les Diablerets / Glacier 3000 (approximately 3 hours by car or train via Chur and Aigle). Take the cable car up to 3,000m and walk across the iconic Peak Walk by Tissot — the world's first suspension bridge connecting two mountain peaks. The 360-degree panoramic views of 24 Alpine peaks including Mont Blanc, the Matterhorn, and the Eiger are absolutely breathtaking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Glacier 3000 summit area — try the Snow Bus (a monster truck ride across the glacier), the alpine coaster, or simply ski/snowboard on the glacier slopes. This is a fantastic final alpine adventure to cap off the week. Descend by cable car in the mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo for your final evening. Enjoy a celebratory farewell dinner in the village, reflecting on an incredible week in the Swiss Alps.

meals.breakfast: Final B&B breakfast at Berninahaus Poschiavo Panorama — savor it as your last morning in this beautiful setting.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Botta 3000 restaurant at the Glacier 3000 summit — a stunning architectural restaurant with panoramic glacier views. Enjoy a mid-range set menu or à la carte. Budget CHF 35–55.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at the best restaurant in Poschiavo — Ristorante Albrici or a local favorite. Treat yourself to a full regional Graubünden meal: barley soup, venison or lamb, and a local Poschiavo dessert. Pair with a glass of local Valtellina red wine. Budget CHF 50–70 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Glacier 3000 cable car tickets cost approximately CHF 45–60 return. The Peak Walk is included in the cable car ticket. Book in advance during peak winter season. If departing Switzerland the following day, confirm your transfer or train connection from Poschiavo to the airport. The Bernina Express to Chur and onward to Zurich Airport is a spectacular final journey — book seats in advance on SBB.ch or RhB.ch. Pack and prepare luggage the night before for an easy morning departure.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival. Flight UA lands at 22:30. Transfer from airport to B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama via private luxury chauffeur service. Check-in and settle into your alpine retreat overlooking the Bernina Pass.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit.
day_by_day.evening: Late-night welcome: Enjoy a pre-arranged private cheese and charcuterie board with a bottle of Valais Pinot Noir waiting in your room, courtesy of the property. Rest and acclimatize to the mountain altitude.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: N/A — in transit
meals.dinner: In-room welcome spread: local Graubünden cured meats, Vacherin cheese, sourdough bread, and Swiss chocolate truffles arranged by the B&B upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance — Poschiavo is approximately 2.5–3 hours from Zurich Airport. Confirm chauffeur pickup at arrivals hall. Keep Day 1 light to recover from travel fatigue and adjust to the 1,800m altitude.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late breakfast at the B&B followed by an orientation walk through the charming historic village of Poschiavo — a UNESCO-listed Italian-speaking enclave in the Swiss Alps. Explore the Piazza da Cumün and the baroque Church of San Vittore. Pick up premium ski gear rental from a local outfitter or use pre-arranged equipment delivery to the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearby Livigno ski area (approx. 45 minutes via the Bernina Pass road) or explore beginner-to-intermediate slopes at Diavolezza-Lagalb ski resort (approx. 20 minutes), one of the most scenic glacier ski areas in the Engadin. Enjoy afternoon skiing with panoramic views of Piz Palü and the Morteratsch Glacier.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo for a refined dinner at Ristorante Suisse or Albergo Croce Federale — both celebrated for their regional Graubünden cuisine. Enjoy pizzoccheri (buckwheat pasta with alpine cheese), venison ragù, and local Poschiavo wine.

meals.breakfast: Full alpine breakfast at B&B Berninahaus: fresh bread, local honey, Engadin nut tart, cold cuts, soft-boiled eggs, and mountain herb tea
meals.lunch: On-mountain lunch at Diavolezza mountain restaurant — panoramic terrace dining with rösti, fondue, and hot chocolate
meals.dinner: Ristorante Suisse, Poschiavo — 3-course regional dinner featuring Graubünden specialties, local wine pairing, and house-made desserts

day_by_day.notes: Check road conditions on the Bernina Pass (SS38/Route 29) before driving — winter tires and chains may be required. Diavolezza-Lagalb ski pass can be purchased online in advance for priority access. Sunset from Diavolezza at approximately 17:45 is spectacular — plan your last run accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early by private transfer or the iconic Bernina Express panoramic train to St. Moritz (approx. 45 minutes by train — one of the most scenic rail journeys in the world). Arrive in St. Moritz and check into a day-use luxury lounge or spa at Badrutt's Palace Hotel or Kulm Hotel for refreshments and preparation.
day_by_day.afternoon: St. Moritz Ice Skating & Bobsled Experience — Skate on the legendary frozen Lake St. Moritz, a glittering natural ice rink at 1,856m altitude. Then experience the historic Cresta Run or the Olympic Bobsled Run — one of the world's oldest and most thrilling bobsled tracks, dating to 1904. Private guided bobsled rides available for premium guests.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Badrutt's Palace Hotel's La Diala or the iconic Chesa Veglia (1658) — St. Moritz's oldest building and most celebrated restaurant, offering wood-fired cuisine, truffle dishes, and an extraordinary wine cellar. Dress code: smart elegant.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at B&B before departure — continental spread with Engadin pastries and espresso
meals.lunch: Lunch at Hanselmann Café & Konditorei, St. Moritz — a legendary institution since 1894, famous for Engadiner Nusstorte, hot chocolate, and open-faced sandwiches
meals.dinner: Chesa Veglia, St. Moritz — 4-course gourmet dinner with truffle risotto, Alpine beef tenderloin, and Grand Cru wine pairing (budget CHF 250–400 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the bobsled experience well in advance — slots are extremely limited and fill up weeks ahead. The Bernina Express is a UNESCO World Heritage railway — reserve first-class panoramic seats. Return to Poschiavo by private transfer in the evening (approx. 45 min).

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to Zermatt Ski Safari — depart by private luxury transfer (approx. 3.5 hours) or take a scenic train combination via Chur and Visp. Arrive in the car-free village of Zermatt, dominated by the iconic Matterhorn. Meet your private ski guide for a personalized ski safari across Zermatt's world-renowned 360km of pistes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Zermatt Ski Safari — access the Klein Matterhorn (3,883m), Europe's highest ski area, via the Matterhorn Glacier Paradise cable car. Ski the legendary Theodul Glacier runs with your expert guide. Optional heli-skiing upgrade available for the ultimate luxury experience. Pause for a vin chaud (mulled wine) at a mountain hut with direct Matterhorn views.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Zermatt at Restaurant Zum See — a legendary mountain restaurant accessible only by ski or snowshoe, serving refined alpine cuisine in a 400-year-old farmhouse. Alternatively, dine at Chez Vrony on the Findeln slope — celebrated for its raclette, local lamb, and Matterhorn panorama. Overnight in Zermatt at The Omnia or Mont Cervin Palace (recommended upgrade for this night).

meals.breakfast: Early grab-and-go breakfast at B&B or en route — croissants, fruit, and thermos coffee for the transfer
meals.lunch: On-mountain lunch at Findlerhof or Chez Vrony — panoramic terrace dining with Matterhorn views, rösti, and alpine cheese fondue
meals.dinner: Restaurant Zum See, Zermatt — intimate 5-course alpine gourmet dinner with local game, truffle, and Swiss wine (reservations essential, book 2–3 weeks ahead)

day_by_day.notes: Zermatt is a car-free village — the final leg from Täsch is by electric taxi or train. Arrange ski equipment rental in Zermatt in advance through your guide service. The Zermatt Ski Safari experience from the available list is the anchor activity for this day — confirm private guide booking before departure.

day_by_day.morning: Morning skiing in Zermatt — take the Gornergrat Bahn (cogwheel railway) to 3,089m for sunrise skiing with unobstructed views of 29 peaks over 4,000m, including Monte Rosa. Ski the quieter morning runs before the slopes fill. Return to Poschiavo by private transfer by early afternoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Traditional Swiss Alpine Cuisine & Cheese Cellar Tour — upon returning to the Poschiavo/Engadin area, join a guided visit to a traditional alpine cheese dairy and cellar. Learn the centuries-old art of Graubünden cheese-making, taste aged Bergkäse, Sbrinz, and Appenzeller varieties, and participate in a hands-on raclette preparation session with a local master cheesemaker.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the B&B — enjoy a private fondue dinner arranged by the property on the terrace or in a cozy alpine dining room, paired with a curated selection of Swiss white wines (Fendant from Valais recommended). Stargazing from the panoramic terrace — Poschiavo's low light pollution makes for extraordinary alpine night skies.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Zermatt (if overnight stay) or early B&B breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Light lunch during cheese cellar tour — artisan bread, fresh cheese curds, cured meats, and local apple juice included in the tour experience
meals.dinner: Private in-house fondue dinner at B&B Berninapass — traditional moitié-moitié (Gruyère & Vacherin) fondue with accompaniments, local wine, and Swiss chocolate dessert

day_by_day.notes: The cheese cellar tour should be pre-booked through a local Engadin agritourism operator or via the B&B concierge. This is the 'Traditional Swiss Alpine Cuisine & Cheese Cellar Tour' from the available experiences list. Confirm return transfer from Zermatt to Poschiavo (approx. 3.5 hours) — depart Zermatt no later than 11:00 to arrive comfortably for the afternoon activity.

day_by_day.morning: Glacier 3000 Suspension Bridge & Peak Walk — depart by private transfer to Les Diablerets (approx. 3 hours from Poschiavo via Chur). Take the cable car up to Glacier 3000 (2,971m) and walk across the Peak Walk by Tissot — the world's first suspension bridge connecting two mountain peaks, offering 360-degree views of 24 four-thousanders including Mont Blanc, the Matterhorn, and the Eiger. A truly once-in-a-lifetime alpine experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Glacier 3000's additional offerings — ski the glacier slopes, try the Snow Bus (a unique snow groomer ride across the glacier), or take the thrilling Alpine Coaster. Optional: dog sledding experience on the glacier plateau. Descend by cable car and begin the scenic return journey toward Poschiavo.
day_by_day.evening: Stop for dinner in Gstaad or Saanen en route — dine at the legendary Chesery Restaurant in Gstaad (one of Switzerland's finest, with 17 Gault Millau points), featuring seasonal alpine cuisine, black truffle dishes, and an exceptional 800-label wine list. Return to Poschiavo by private transfer.

meals.breakfast: Full B&B breakfast before early departure — eggs, local cold cuts, Engadin pastries, fresh juice, and mountain herb tea
meals.lunch: Glacier 3000 Summit Restaurant — panoramic glass-enclosed dining at nearly 3,000m with hot soups, mountain pasta, and warm drinks
meals.dinner: Restaurant Chesery, Gstaad — 4-course gourmet dinner with seasonal alpine ingredients, truffle and game specialties, and Grand Cru wine pairing (CHF 300–500 per person; reservations essential)

day_by_day.notes: Glacier 3000 is the featured 'Glacier 3000 Suspension Bridge & Peak Walk' experience from the available list. Book cable car tickets and Peak Walk access online in advance — weekends can be busy. The round trip from Poschiavo is long (approx. 6–7 hours driving total) — a private driver is strongly recommended. Confirm Chesery reservation at least 2 weeks in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Jungfrau Region Snowshoeing & Winter Hiking — depart by private transfer or Bernina Express + connecting trains to Grindelwald or Wengen in the Jungfrau region (approx. 3.5–4 hours). Join a guided snowshoeing tour through pristine alpine landscapes beneath the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau. Trek through snow-laden forests, frozen meadows, and dramatic glacier viewpoints with a certified mountain guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ascend to Jungfraujoch — 'Top of Europe' (3,454m) via the historic cogwheel railway for a final panoramic alpine experience. Visit the Ice Palace, walk on the Aletsch Glacier (the longest glacier in the Alps), and enjoy the observation deck views. Descend and begin the return journey to Poschiavo for your final evening.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the B&B or at a celebrated local restaurant in Poschiavo — Ristorante Albergo Croce Federale or a private chef dinner arranged by the B&B. Celebrate the week with a special Swiss tasting menu: Bündner Gerstensuppe (barley soup), venison medallions with chanterelles, Engadin nut tart, and a bottle of aged Pinot Noir from Graubünden. Pack and prepare for departure.

meals.breakfast: Early full breakfast at B&B before departure — hearty alpine spread to fuel the snowshoeing day
meals.lunch: Jungfraujoch Crystal Restaurant or Aletsch Restaurant at the Top of Europe — panoramic dining at 3,454m with hot alpine dishes and celebratory Champagne toast
meals.dinner: Farewell private chef dinner at B&B Berninahaus or Ristorante Albergo Croce Federale — 5-course Graubünden tasting menu with wine pairing and Swiss chocolate petit fours

day_by_day.notes: This day combines the 'Jungfrau Region Snowshoeing & Winter Hiking' experience from the available list with a Jungfraujoch visit. Book Jungfraujoch railway tickets well in advance — they sell out quickly, especially on weekends. Snowshoeing guide should be pre-booked through Jungfrau Region tourism. Confirm departure logistics for Day 8 — arrange private transfer to airport or train station the evening before. Tip: purchase a Swiss Travel Pass for unlimited train travel if using public transport throughout the week.
